chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from Amr ibn Sa'id, from Musaddiq ibn Sadah, from 'Ammar al-Sabati, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about Al-Fuqqa' (a type of fermented drink), and he said: 'It is wine (khamr).'

key_terms.أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah, a common title for Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him).
key_terms.الْفُقَّاع: A specific type of fermented drink, often made from grains or fruits, mentioned in this context as an intoxicant.
key_terms.خَمْر: Wine or an intoxicating drink; the primary category for prohibited fermented beverages in Islamic jurisprudence.
key_terms.عَنِ: From/About; used here to indicate the subject of inquiry.

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on drinking Fuqqa' according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Istibsar establishes the legal ruling on 'Al-Fuqqa'', a specific fermented beverage, with multiple narrations from the Imams confirming its prohibition. While Imam al-Sadiq (AS) explicitly classifies it as 'khamr', Imam al-Rida (AS) provides deeper jurisprudential nuance, stating it is 'unknown' khamr and asserting that if he held absolute authority, he would execute its seller and flog its drinker, indicating a ruling of 'khamr majhul' (unknown wine) with the hadd penalty of the drinker. This highlights the Shia scholarly distinction between definite intoxicants and those whose intoxicating properties are not universally recognized but are still treated with severe caution.
